headline: High-risk default overlap: shared filesystem, broad egress, and auto-execute-capable IDE workflows create dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes workflow artifacts and exposes files/stdin-stdout; Agent B uses clipboard, workspace files, and MCP, and its shared_state_with_other_instances is via local filesystem. That creates a default bridge where attacker-controlled content from A can be parsed by B as instructions. The interaction is documented enough to judge, but the shared filesystem plus MCP raises this above low.
conditions: IF Agent A writes untrusted workflow output into shared workspace files
IF Agent B ingests workspace or clipboard content as instructions or tool context
IF an MCP server is connected to Agent B without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate A and B into different workspaces
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Require provenance tags on files before B reads them
Restrict B MCP servers to allowlisted tools
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization before B parses A outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches database, cloud storage, logs, messages, and notifications, while Agent B reads workspace files and sends context to a model proxy/MCP servers with broad egress. If A places sensitive data into shared files or outputs, B can forward it off-box by default. This is a realistic leakage path in the pair, not just an unusual setup.
conditions: IF Agent A writes logs, database data, or cloud-storage data into the shared workspace
IF Agent B sends workspace content to its model proxy or an MCP server
IF both agents operate under the same local filesystem permissions
mitigations: Move sensitive A outputs out of B's workspace
Disable B access to shared files containing secrets
Use separate OS users for A and B
Audit MCP servers for outbound data handling
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data-class labels and blocking rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Agent B can also write the filesystem, modify git state, and uses shared_state_with_other_instances via local filesystem. Both therefore have overlapping write authority on the same mutable surfaces, and B's git operations make conflicts and corruption plausible by default. Uncertainty is low because both profiles explicitly expose the overlap.
conditions: IF A and B target the same directory or repository
IF B modifies git state while A writes files concurrently
IF no external lock or transaction layer is present
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to A and B
Pause one agent during git operations
Use file locks around shared mutable paths
Run B with git disabled for shared repos
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A produces workflow artifacts, logs, and notifications; Agent B is an IDE agent with MCP and auto-execute opt-in, so A's outputs can become B's actionable input. Because B can execute commands and modify git state, a mistaken or malicious A output can cascade into irreversible code or repo changes. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF B treats A-generated files or messages as authoritative
IF B auto-execute is enabled or commands are approved without review
IF A emits malformed or adversarial workflow instructions
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A outputs
Disable auto-execute in B
Route A outputs through a validation step
Limit B to read-only mode for A-produced artifacts
requires-engineering: add schema validation for A-to-B handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles cloud storage data, database data, messages, and notifications, while Agent B handles source code and open files with broad egress and closed-source vendor processing. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because uncertainty remains, the higher plausible severity is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data from A is written into B-opened files
IF B sends those files to its model proxy or MCP servers
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not documented here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B workspaces
Review vendor retention settings before use
Disable syncing of sensitive files into the IDE
Use redacted test data for shared workflows
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
